When Steve Jobs formed Apple, computers were things only used by a few individuals in corporations. By making a reasonably affordable desktop computer, computers could be on the desks of all individuals in corporations, then that spread to all companies and businesses, including small businesses, and classrooms, and ultimately, the household.

The Internet pretty much cemented domestic use of computers, and Apple had to now appeal to both business and home users in different ways. They evolved.

Later, Apple saw that portable devices (not laptops) and wearables were going to be the way things were going and made the iPod (and changed the music industry), the iPhone (changing the cellphone industry and defining the standard for smartphones), the iPad (killed off netbooks), and the Apple Watch. Facetime popularized video calling because it was simple and available on virtually any Apple device.

Apple also popularized e-books, podcasts, and made devices that made it easy to record photos and videos, killing off digital cameras and camcorders (except for pros).

Apple's digital downloads for TV and movies got the ball rolling with Digital video file sale/rental/distribution industry.

So between Apple's founding and today, they've made computing something that exclusive to a few people in a large corporation to something people have in their pocket or wrist, and launched digital frontiers for music, movies, books, and TV. I'd say they've done well and continue to evolve with the times.
